t:
Section 834 of title 10, United States Code (article 34 of the Uniform Code of Military Justice), is amended to read as follows:“§ 834. Art. 34. Advice to convening authority before referral for trial“(a) General Court-martial.—“(1) Staff judge advocate advice required before referral.—Before referral of charges and specifications to a general court-martial for trial, the convening authority shall submit the matter to the staff judge advocate for advice, which the staff judge advocate shall provide to the convening authority in writing. The convening authority may not refer a specification under a charge to a general court-martial unless the staff judge advocate advises the convening authority in writing that—“(A) the specification alleges an offense under this chapter;“(B) there is probable cause to believe that the accused committed the offense charged; and“(C) a court-martial would have jurisdiction over the accused and the offense.“(2) Staff judge advocate recommendation as to disposition.—Together with the written advice provided under paragraph (1), the staff judge advocate shall provide a written recommendation to the convening authority as to the disposition that should be made of the specification in the interest of justice and discipline.“(3) Staff judge advocate advice and recommendation to accompany referral.—When a convening authority makes a referral for trial by general court-martial, the written advice of the staff judge advocate under paragraph (1) and the written recommendation of the staff judge advocate under paragraph (2) with respect to each specification shall accompany the referral.“(b) Special Court-martial; Convening Authority Consultation With Judge Advocate.—Before referral of charges and specifications to a special court-martial for trial, the convening authority shall consult a judge advocate on relevant legal issues.“(c) General and Special Courts-martial; Correction of Charges and Specifications Before Referral.—Before referral for trial by general court-martial or special court-martial, changes may be made to charges and specifications—“(1) to correct errors in form; and“(2) when applicable, to conform to the substance of the evidence contained in a report under section 832(c) of this title (article 32(c)).“(d) Referral Defined.—In this section, the term ‘referral’ means the order of a convening authority that charges and specifications against an accused be tried by a specified court-martial.”
.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that the mandatory "advice" and "consult" language before a referral decision amounts to participation. But the convening authority, the staff judge advocate, and the judge advocate are all military officers inside the federal government, so this is purely intra-government consultation. No state, tribe, expert, member of the public, or other outside party is brought into the decision, and no right to sue or rulemaking is created.
fable.s: Before referral of charges and specifications to a special court-martial for trial, the convening authority shall consult a judge advocate on relevant legal issues.

qwen_block.w: The section requires a convening authority (a military officer) to consult with a staff judge advocate (a military lawyer) before referring charges to a court-martial. Both the convening authority and the staff judge advocate are federal employees/officers within the Department of Defense. Therefore, this is intra-governmental coordination, not participation by an outside party.
qwen_block.s: the convening authority shall submit the matter to the staff judge advocate for advice, which the staff judge advocate shall provide to the convening authority in writing

opus.w: The section does require consultation before a referral decision, but everyone in that consultation (the convening authority, the staff judge advocate and the judge advocate) is a military official inside the federal government. Consultation within the government is not participation. No state, expert, member of the public or other outside party has a role, and no right to sue or object is granted.
opus.s: Before referral of charges and specifications to a special court-martial for trial, the convening authority shall consult a judge advocate on relevant legal issues.
opus.b: The tempting reading is that this counts as participation because it requires advice and consultation ("shall submit the matter to the staff judge advocate for advice", "shall consult a judge advocate") before a decision is made. That reading fails because the convening authority, the staff judge advocate and the judge advocate are all military officers, so they are all inside the federal government. No outside party is involved.

qwen_chat.w: This section requires a convening authority (a federal official) to consult with a staff judge advocate (a federal employee) before referring charges to a court-martial. Since both the convening authority and the staff judge advocate are part of the federal government, this is intra-governmental coordination, not participation by an outside party. The definition explicitly excludes consultation between federal officials or employees.
qwen_chat.s: Before referral of charges and specifications to a general court-martial for trial, the convening authority shall submit the matter to the staff judge advocate for advice, which the staff judge advocate shall provide to the convening authority in writing.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that the "staff judge advocate" or "judge advocate" is an outside expert providing advice, thus constituting participation. However, staff judge advocates and judge advocates are federal employees (military officers) within the Department of Defense. The definition explicitly states that consultation or coordination between federal officials or employees is "intra-government coordination" and does not count as participation. The convening authority is also a federal official. Therefore, all actors involved are inside the federal government.
